diagnosis: The cube_stack baseline never grasps the red cube: after sampling a grasp pose and moving to it with goto_pose (step 3), the program immediately lifts (step 4) without ever closing the gripper. Every primitive returns status 'ok' because none fails in isolation, so the trace shows no FAILURES; the defect is a broken causal chain, not a primitive error. The keyframe after the lift (seed0_step004_goto_pose_after.png) confirms it visually — the arm has risen but the red cube is still resting on the table, i.e. an open-gripper 'air' pick. Consequently the subsequent transport-to-green, open_gripper, and retract all operate on an empty gripper and nothing is stacked, yielding zero reward across all debugging seeds. The fix inserts a single close_gripper() call between reaching the grasp pose and the lift; validated at score 1.0 on debugging seeds 0, 1, and 2.

proposed_skills.name: close-gripper-before-lift
proposed_skills.failure_signature: Pick-and-place program reaches the sampled grasp pose and lifts, but the object stays on the table (post-lift keyframe shows empty gripper); all primitives report 'ok' / zero FAILURES yet task reward is 0 because the object is never transported.
proposed_skills.when_to_apply: Any pick-transport-place task where the code sequence is sample_grasp_pose -> goto_pose(grasp) -> goto_pose(lift) with no gripper-closing primitive between the descent and the lift.
proposed_skills.strategy: After moving the end-effector to the grasp pose (goto_pose to the sampled grasp position), issue close_gripper() to actually secure the object before any lifting/transport goto_pose. A successful grasp should leave a non-trivial gripper width; verify from the trace that the lift keyframe shows the object moving with the gripper rather than remaining on the surface.
proposed_skills.code_sketch:
pick_pos, pick_quat = sample_grasp_pose(obj)
goto_pose(pick_pos, pick_quat, z_approach=0.1)
close_gripper()  # secure object before lifting
lift = pick_pos.copy(); lift[2] += 0.2
goto_pose(lift, pick_quat)
